content:
Two years ago, when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports brought welcome news: the built-in SSD was not soldered to the motherboard. This allowed users to upgrade storage capacity after purchase, and we even demonstrated how to do it at the time.

However, after the new-generation M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini updates, the storage chips appear to be soldered to the motherboard once again.

New Mac mini storage chips soldered back on, seen as a step backwards

Expand Mac mini noted in a blog post that the NAND chips are soldered directly to the motherboard, similar to the M1 and M2 versions of the Mac mini, meaning the SSD modules cannot be removed.

Expand Mac mini has been selling storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini. However, according to what they are currently saying, 'the chances of supporting the M6 and M5 Pro do not look optimistic.'

With no slot, there's nothing to swap out, and the room for us to make a difference is very limited. Back in August this year we mentioned that we would need to test the actual hardware before expanding our support. Now the test results are out, and it's not the outcome we were hoping for. We will keep looking for ways to break through, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro seems unlikely. If circumstances change, we will let everyone know here first thing.

For comparison, Expand Mac mini's 1TB SSD expansion module for the M4 Mac mini is priced at USD 300. Apple charges USD 500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module sells for USD 420, while Apple's upgrade fee is USD 1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guides still show that the SSD can be removed. We have not yet seen any teardown reports that can confirm this.

If you are using an M4 Mac mini and want to upgrade the storage, you can follow the detailed tutorial produced by Jeff Benjamin from 9to5Mac step by step.

Although it is not a direct internal storage upgrade, Satechi has launched a rather ingenious accessory that includes a built-in SSD enclosure and additionally provides multiple ports, designed specifically for the M6 Mac mini.
